memories.context: DeepAgents (Atlas) is an autonomous multi-agent studio system producing high-fidelity audiovisual content from concepts. Core architecture: LangGraph orchestration with Postgres checkpointing, LanceDB for semantic storage, Streamlit GUI with asyncio bridge. Intelligence: Google Gemini 2.0 Flash (primary). Media: Replicate for Audio/Video/Image. Ontology-driven agents: Director (Apollo), Researcher (Delphi), Confidence (Editor), Cinematographer (Lumiere), Composer (Orpheus). Zero-Touch philosophy with Hub-first configuration from LangSmith. The Jewel Standard mandates 10/10 linting.
decisions: Google Gemini 2.0 Flash as primary LLM (high quota)
LangSmith Hub as single source of truth for config
Postgres for state, LanceDB for semantic memory
rationale: Gemini 2.0 Flash has higher RPM/TPM than Claude
Hub-first enables runtime config changes without code deployment
Fail-Fast makes debugging trivial vs hidden errors
Hybrid persistence separates concerns (OLTP vs Vector)

memories.context: Created DeepAgents/services/ package for zero-touch UI configuration. SchemaService fetches OpenAPI schemas from Replicate API, parses to ControlDefinition objects. DynamicUIGenerator creates Streamlit widgets (sliders/selects/checkboxes) from schemas. ModelRegistry contains curated catalog of 15+ AI models (video/music/voice/image). GUI sections: Cinematographer and Composer with active checkboxes, model dropdowns, dynamic parameter expanders. Config flows: GUI -> AgentRunner -> Graph -> Agent nodes. Features: voice dependency resolution, storyboard option, green/red validation indicators.
decisions: Services package architecture with schema_service.py, ui_generator.py, asset_validator.py, model_registry.py
Memory + disk caching for schemas (24-hour TTL)
ModelProvider enum (REPLICATE, VERTEX_AI, GOOGLE_GENAI) for provider awareness
rationale: Provider enum allows skipping schema fetch for non-Replicate models

memories.context: All agent nodes in StateGraph return Command[Literal[...]] instead of plain state dicts. HANDOFF Protocol: delegation tools return 'HANDOFF:agent_name:directive' strings parsed from ToolMessage content. Node functions route dynamically via Command(update={...}, goto=handoff[0]). No add_conditional_edges() - all routing decisions made dynamically by Command returns. Agent-specific tool sets: DIRECTOR_TOOLS, COMPOSER_TOOLS, CINEMATOGRAPHER_TOOLS, EDITOR_TOOLS from inter_agent_comms.py. This enables true emergent agent collaboration without brittle hardcoded routing.
decisions: Curated tool sets per agent role

memories.topic: FFmpeg Stream Copy for Lossless Media Merging
memories.context: MoviePy re-encodes video during merging causing quality degradation. Gold Standard: FFmpeg stream copy (-c:v copy) for bit-for-bit video preservation. Command pattern: ffmpeg -y -i video.mp4 -i audio.mp3 -c:v copy -c:a aac -b:a 192k -map 0:v:0 -map 1:a:0 -shortest output.mp4. Fallback chain: FFmpeg CLI -> ffmpeg-python -> MoviePy. Key functions: merge_ffmpeg_stream_copy(), quick_merge(), concat_videos_ffmpeg(). FFmpeg 8.0+ required on PATH (install via winget). Stream copy is instant with zero quality loss vs MoviePy's slow re-encoding.
decisions: FFmpeg CLI as primary merge method
Fallback to MoviePy only for complex filters
rationale: Order of magnitude faster than re-encoding

memories.context: LangGraph CLI on Windows encounters BlockingIOError (WinError 183) during file operations. Workaround: ALL local dev servers MUST run with --allow-blocking. Additional: --no-reload prevents unnecessary restarts. Start with: python -m langgraph_cli dev --port 2024 --no-browser --allow-blocking --no-reload. CRITICAL: Set PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 to prevent Unicode crashes. VS Code terminals cause premature exit - use Start-Job for background isolation. Server startup takes 50-65 seconds due to google.api_core packages_distributions() scan.
rationale: Windows cp1252 crashes on Unicode emoji

memories.context: LangSmith Hub is Source of Truth for system config. Local cache (DeepAgents/.cache/prompts/) exists ONLY for startup speed. When model/config issues occur: 1) Check LangSmith Hub for current config, 2) Verify local cache matches Hub, 3) If mismatch: delete cache and restart OR run push_config_fix.py to sync. Model ID format: Replicate uses provider/owner/model (e.g., replicate/wan-video/wan-2.5-t2v-fast). Parser splits on first / only. Zero-Touch Prompt Management: prompts.py tries CLIENT.pull_prompt(repo), falls back to CLIENT.push_prompt(repo, local_default) if 404.
decisions: Hub is authoritative, cache is optimization only
rationale: Prevents config drift between local and remote
Prompts editable by non-coders in Hub

memories.topic: Forced Tool Execution Pattern for Media Agents
memories.context: LLM agents hallucinate tool calls - outputting text descriptions instead of actually calling tools. Solution: Use tool_choice='any' when binding tools to force actual execution. Apply to all media generation agents (Cinematographer, Composer) that MUST call external APIs. Add [TOOL BINDING] log messages to confirm tool_choice is active. This prevents 'air guitar' behavior where agents describe what they would do rather than doing it.
rationale: Forces actual API calls over descriptions
Makes debugging easier with explicit logs

memories.context: ModelRegistry in services/model_registry.py contains curated AI models. Categories: VIDEO (Wan 2.5 Fast, Luma Ray Flash 2, Minimax Video-01, Veo 3.1 Fast), AUDIO_MUSIC (Lyria-002, ACE-Step, Minimax Music-01, MusicGen), AUDIO_VOICE (Minimax Speech-01, XTTS-v2, Kokoro), IMAGE (FLUX Schnell/Pro, SDXL, SDXL Lightning, Imagen 3). ModelProvider enum: REPLICATE, VERTEX_AI, GOOGLE_GENAI. is_replicate property for provider checking. Schema fetching skipped for non-Replicate models. Cost tracking with cost_per_run and cost_unit fields.
rationale: Curated list ensures quality and compatibility
Provider awareness prevents wrong API calls

memories.context: Primary: Minimax Music-1.5 for full songs with lyrics (600 char limit, variable duration). Fallback: MusicGen for instrumental only (explicit duration control, max 30s). High Density prompting strategy: compression over truncation to fit full song arc in API budget. Phase-Based Classification pattern: PHASE 1 (Audit/Classify) then PHASE 2 (Execute) prevents lyric hallucinations in instrumental requests. Linear Chain pattern (Reason -> Tool -> Stop) prevents overthinking after generation.

Director Agent role: Pure generation of textual plans (Creative Directives). MUST NOT have access to tools (validate_scene_logic, assemble_final_cut). Tool access causes GraphRecursionError from infinite validation loops. Prompt engineering: explicitly forbid 'reviewing' or 'summarizing' - must output plan directly. YOU ARE THE AUTHOR instructions prevent meta-review hallucinations. Director produces text-only plans routed by Graph, not executed via internal tools.
decisions: Strict YOU ARE THE AUTHOR prompting

memories.topic: VS Code Extension Crashes Root Cause Analysis
memories.context: VS Code experiencing repeated crashes (3 dumps in 10 minutes). Root cause: Listener memory leak - '[172] potential listener LEAK detected, having 223 listeners already'. Pattern: tool invocations add listeners not cleaned up, accumulate to ~223+, VS Code becomes unstable and crashes. Problematic extensions: MemoriPilot (trying to register 4 chatParticipants not in package.json), Mermaid Chart (requesting non-existent API proposal). Solution: Disable problematic extensions, restart VS Code to reset listener count.
decisions: Identified listener leak as crash cause
Migration to Flowbaby for memory management
rationale: Undeclared chatParticipants cause VS Code errors
